Web host, Blazor shell, REST, MCP, and command line for local tools built on the NetworkInspector base.

The UI-free core of a base application: identity, typed commands with one pipeline, a license gate, generic plugins, settings and profiles, messages and a log file, jobs, texts in several languages, shared UI state, and row sources for huge growing lists. It references no web or desktop framework.
Desktop window for applications on NetworkInspector.BaseApp: the same UI in an Avalonia window with the operating system's WebView (WebView2, WKWebView, WebKitGTK).

Jobs for any .NET application: asynchronous or blocking work with a state, allocation-free progress, a cooperative cancel, a bounded list of ended jobs, and a bounded stop of all jobs. It depends only on NetworkInspector.Limits.

License inventory for any .NET application: one entry per shipped component with license, holder, and text; a strict JSON form; reading an inventory embedded in an assembly with a size bound; and a SHA-256 hash that names exactly what a person accepted. It depends on nothing but the .NET runtime.

Build-time license inventory for .NET applications and plugins: determines license, holder, and text of every shipped package, project, framework, and asset offline from the restore output, embeds them as NetworkInspector.Licenses.json, and fails the build when a fact is unknown.
Generic plugin contract: entry and host requirement attributes, semantic version, plugin module and kind interfaces, builder stage, context, and log.
Network Inspector's plugin contribution registry: staging builder, stack and settings contributions, sources, exporters, and export target rules.

Keryx.Broadcast: shared-socket broadcast fan-out transport for the Keryx WebRTC stack. A BroadcastEndpoint serves many viewers over one UDP socket, demuxing inbound datagrams to per-viewer sessions by 5-tuple with STUN first-contact binding, so per-ingest-packet fan-out can batch on a single socket.
